about: First-hop redundancy on routers: two or more routers on one LAN share a virtual gateway address; the highest priority owns it, and a backup takes over when it falls silent. Set up per interface with `vrrp GROUP ...`.

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.GROUP: Group number, the same on every router of the group (1 to 255)
help.address: The virtual address hosts use as their gateway
help.ADDRESS: An unused address on this interface's subnet

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.priority: Who wins the election: the higher number (default 100; 255 means this router owns the address)

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.interval: Seconds between the master's announcements (default 1; every router of the group must agree)

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.preempt: Take the address back from a lower-priority master (the default)

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.preempt: Stay backup even with a higher priority until the master fails

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.virtual-mac: Answer ARP for the address with the group's own MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:GROUP instead of the interface's MAC

help.vrrp: Shared gateway address with other routers
help.virtual-mac: Use the interface's own MAC again (the default)

help.vrrp: Leave the group and forget its settings
Each group: its state, who is master, priority and timers
